prompt: Think back to your first week with Vantage: inviting or being invited, signing in with a CAC, the consent banner, setting rank and MOS. What almost stopped you, and what made you keep going?
On a normal day, what do you actually do in Vantage: claim cases, follow the procedure, Quick Log, hand off? What do you still do in a spreadsheet or email instead, and why?
How are the workload counts used in your section? Has anyone been judged or ranked by them, and did the definitions and the three-person rule on totals change how people felt about it?
When JEPES came due, did the Record and the billet accomplishments it wrote help? What was missing, wrong, or not trusted by the chain?

If you were promoted to Sergeant or wrote a fitness report, how did the switch to FITREP input, the Section C draft and the MRO worksheet blocks go? Did the input reach the reporting senior on time, and was it credible?
When someone transferred or the reporting senior changed, what happened to their work, their credit and their access? Was anything lost, misattributed or visible to the wrong people?
When the monthly personnel extract separated people, what went right or wrong? Did anyone take their record with them at EAS?
From where you sit, would Vantage pass an ISSM review and a records request years from now? What worries you about audit, retention or who can read what?
If you could change one thing about Vantage to make the section use it for the whole enlistment, what would it be?
